source.title: How Spurious Features are Memorized: Precise Analysis for Random and NTK Features

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and additional neural network architectures, measuring how spurious-feature memorization changes with test accuracy and dataset size. This bears on generalization, but does not test the listed claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper measures test accuracy and spurious accuracy across training-set sizes and activation functions. Those results concern memorization of irrelevant input features, not fitting random labels, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons for natural-label generalization, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Theoretical bounds and cited prior results are not separate experimental rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures memorization of irrelevant input features and its relationship to sample size, activation choice and generalization. It does not test any listed version: input-feature memorization is different from fitting random labels or selectively removing memorized examples. The separate FC and CNN experiments provide no readable comparative result establishing V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately reflects the authors' conclusion: stability and feature alignment characterize irrelevant-feature memorization, with RF/NTK theory and experiments linking weaker memorization to better generalization. However, 'proportional to generalization error' should be attributed to the authors: equations 4.4, 5.5 and 6.5 give covariance upper bounds involving the square root of generalization error, rather than an exact proportionality for spurious accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies spurious input-feature memorization in random-feature and NTK regression, with numerical experiments extending to standard datasets and fully connected, convolutional, and ResNet models; it does not use the claim's interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported spurious accuracy varies with training-set size, spurious-feature fraction α, activation function, and dataset/model setting; test accuracy is stated to increase with training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the reported sample-size experiments, test accuracy improves while accuracy on queries retaining training noise decreases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the studied models and datasets, increasing training-set size reduces memorization of irrelevant input features while improving generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Spurious accuracy increases with irrelevant-feature fraction α; higher-order activation coefficients reduce memorization. Synthetic test accuracy is reported as insensitive to α and the tested activation choices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization of irrelevant input features depends on feature overlap and activation choice even when held-out accuracy changes little.

record.problems: Experimental accuracy values are presented in figures without tabulated numbers. Most datasets are described as subsets or binary tasks; the experiments measure accuracy and spurious accuracy rather than the training-to-test error gap in the claim versions. The theoretical results rely on stated distribution, over-parameterization, and activation assumptions.

untested.parts: No comparison of natural-label generalization with fitting and held-out performance on fixed random labels.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No established comparative result on convolutional versus fully connected test error, local connectivity, learned sparsity or convolutional initialization.
No optimizer comparison or tuning-budget intervention.
No batch-size comparison, fixed-epoch penalty or compensating training recipe.
No dropout or joint dropout and weight-decay removal comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization gaps.
No selective removal of highly memorized examples followed by retraining and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are relative to V1–V8; cannot_determine does not negate the explicitly stated trends for the separate spurious-feature phenomenon. Figure 6 contains additional experiments outside these versions, so their omission does not require a version-bearing missing entry. The supplied text preserves figure captions and axes but not readable curves.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not compare fitting random labels with natural labels or report chance accuracy on held-out random labels.
It does not sweep fully connected network width beyond the interpolation threshold or measure test error as a function of width.
It includes fully connected, convolutional, and ResNet experiments, but does not compare their natural-label test errors against each other or isolate local connectivity's contribution.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison is reported.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch penalty is tested.
No dropout or weight-decay intervention is tested.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or competing generalization measures are evaluated.
No examples are removed based on memorization or compared with random-example removal.
